task.title: Stop cancelling in-progress CI runs for pushes to main
task.description:
PR #28's .github/workflows/ci.yml:9-11 sets:

  concurrency:
    group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
    cancel-in-progress: true

For pull_request events this is correct and desirable: github.ref is per-PR, so pushing a fixup cancels the now-stale run for that same PR and saves runner minutes.

For push events to main it is wrong. Every push to main shares the group key ci-CI-refs/heads/main, so merging two pull requests back to back cancels the first merge commit's run mid-flight. That commit is then left with a cancelled status, which is neither a pass nor a failure. If PR A was verified against a base that PR B subsequently changed, the semantic conflict between them lands on main with no run that ever verified the resulting tree, and nothing in the UI marks it as unverified.

This defeats part of the point of WB-01KZBT4D9E9V7A5A70G1SNHB7W, which is to guarantee that main is continuously verified rather than spot-checked by hand.

Conventional fix, one line:

  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

Deferred from PR #28 review as a minor finding: it requires two merges in quick succession to trigger, the repo currently has a single developer merging serially, and the acceptance criteria say nothing about concurrency behavior. Worth fixing before the project opens to outside contributors, since that is exactly when back-to-back merges start happening.
